audience: JAX research engineers reading a reusable experiment preparation
scope: Only the three supplied prose files were read. No factual/source audit, code inspection, edits, or publication. Source preparation and CPU/abstract checks are distinct from target execution and adoption.

findings.title: Define the captured X and G tensors
findings.finding: X and G are introduced only as symbols. The supplied prose never identifies what model quantity each denotes or where it is captured. The reported shapes, record counts, and equality therefore cannot tell a fresh reader what scientific comparison was prepared or what the CPU check observed.
findings.minimalCorrection: Define X and G at first use, including their capture location and what the reported record counts count.

findings.title: Identify what distinguishes the legacy and native variants
findings.finding: Legacy/native names label the central cross-branch comparison, but neither branch is defined in any supplied document. The report makes clear that these are separate from the untouched/instrumented axis, yet does not say which implementation or layout choice changes between them. A reader cannot recover the experiment being compared from the names alone.
findings.minimalCorrection: Add one sentence identifying the legacy/native implementation distinction and confirming that both are exercised in untouched and instrumented children.

findings.title: Resolve the source A baseline
findings.finding: The only environment delta is stated relative to source A, while the only named and pinned source in the supplied prose is S2. No sentence identifies source A or its relationship to S2 and the original full fixture. The baseline for the unchanged-scientific-environment claim is therefore unrecoverable.
findings.minimalCorrection: Identify source A with a concrete pin or linked frozen record, and state its relationship to S2.

findings.title: Name the boolean whose False/True values describe capture transport
findings.finding: The phrases global False transport, full-manual local False transport, and per-device collector True identity do not name the boolean argument or explain its meaning. A JAX engineer cannot infer which callback/collection behavior is being asserted from bare booleans; the surrounding identity-custom-VJP statement does not resolve this.
findings.minimalCorrection: Name the exact flag and briefly state what its false and true values mean for these capture paths.

evidenceBoundaryAssessment: The supplied prose explicitly separates local CPU validation and abstract tracing from full-target numerical acceptance, physical evidence, dispatch, performance, and adoption. No finding challenges the truth of source or test claims.
